label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**@Tolu_Aspirant — good evening. Sorry I took a day to reply, I wanted to answer properly because you're asking honest questions and the thread so far has given you two people saying "do this" and "do that" without a single one of them being where you are.**

I'm exactly who you're asking for. 100L Biology, federal university in Lagos. I wrote JAMB 2025, scored 251, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and the portal gave me Biology. So nothing I'm about to say comes from someone who has never sat where you're sitting.

I'll answer your questions in order, and I'll tell you where I'm guessing and where you have to go and check for yourself.

---

**First: can you actually transfer? Yes. Is it automatic? No.**

This is where I'll have to disagree with @Kingsley_MLS respectfully. Transfer is not a myth, but it is also not a shortcut, and I think both "it's a myth" and "just read hard" are lazy answers.

What our level adviser told us when we asked (the 100L people in my department, end of last session):

- You need a **CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5** after 100L
- There must be **space** — i.e. vacancies in Medicine for the year
- You must have met **your school's cut-off for Medicine in JAMB** and the **post-UTME** requirement

On that last one, @Tolu, this is the part I need you to check carefully. You said 268, but 268 on its own does not make you eligible for transfer — Medicine cut-offs in Lagos schools sit somewhere between 260 and 280+ depending on the school and the year, and your post-UTME score matters separately. I don't know your university's cut-offs and I don't know your post-UTME score, so please don't take my word for anything here. Go and ask.

The other number that should tell you what you're actually dealing with: our adviser said **about 6 people moved into Medicine from the whole faculty last year**, and her estimate was that **over 40 applied**. So roughly one in seven. That's not "impossible," but it is definitely not "just read hard and it happens."

And I'll be honest about my own position: **my CGPA after first semester is 4.31.** I'm below 4.5. I'm still pushing, but I'm not going to stand here and tell you it's easy when I'm personally currently under the bar.

---

**Second: how is 100L Biology really? Because nobody in this thread has told you.**

The courses are **BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101, and GST**. The honest truth is that **PHY 101 and MTH 101 are the ones dealing with people.** Physics and Maths have a way of breaking people in 100L, more than the Biology itself. If you're good at those two, 100L Biology is manageable. If they're your weakness, you need to start finding help now — don't wait until the exam.

**The cost of practicals is real, by the way.** Lab coat was 6,500 naira, dissecting kit 9k, plus money for the practical manual. Nobody warns you about that. If your family is tight, ask the department about alternatives before you budget for it.

**How I felt when I saw it:** the day I checked the portal and saw Biology, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried and didn't eat. I was honestly gutted. My mum was still telling people in church that I'm doing medicine for **two months** before she finally stopped — I had to beg her. I remember thinking, this is the end of everything.

**But here's the part I didn't expect.** We did our first BIO practical and dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine, and I actually enjoyed it. That was the first moment I thought, *wait, I might actually like this.* And right now I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected to. Biology is not a bad course. It's genuinely interesting.

But Tolu, I want to be careful here, because this is where I might mislead you. The reason I ended up okay is partly because my own expectations shifted. If you're in 100L Biology refusing to do anything except count down to your transfer application, you'll be miserable. If you're in 100L Biology actually trying to become a good biologist **and** keeping your CGPA above 4.5, you'll have a much better chance at both.

---

**Third: what about rewriting? Is it wrong?**

No, it is not wrong. @favour.o is right that staying at home is not as easy as people say — I have watched people sit at home and slowly lose the energy, the routine, the confidence. That is real and I won't pretend it isn't.

But rewriting is also not a small thing, and I want you to see it clearly before you choose it. The example I think about: **my secondary school classmate, Ifeoma.** She had a Pharmacy offer. She rejected it to rewrite for Medicine. She has now written JAMB **twice more**. She is still at home.

That's not a scare story about rewriting in general. It's a reminder that JAMB is an exam you can fail repeatedly, and that the difference between "one year at home" and "two years at home" is enormous. If you rewrite, rewrite because you genuinely believe you can get the Medicine score in one more attempt — not because a aunty said so on a Tuesday.

Also, @Tolu, one practical thing: **the acceptance deadline is two weeks. Do not pay that fee yet.** Nothing is lost by waiting two weeks. Get the actual transfer rules first, then decide, then pay. And even if you accept Biology now, accepting doesn't legally trap you — you can still write JAMB in a later year — but check JAMB's own rules on candidates who have already registered in a university, because that's the part people mess up.

---

**Fourth: the actual question nobody wants to ask you.**

You said your dad says accept, your aunty says reject. Both of them are guessing about your future, and honestly, both of them are partly right. But it's your life.

So please ask yourself this, and sit with it for a few days: **do you want to be a doctor, or do you want your parents to say their daughter is a doctor?** I'm serious. Those are two different things.

Because if it's mostly the title and the family expectation — I say this with love — then there are other roads where you still become a respected professional, you don't have to suffer, and everybody still gets to tell their relatives "our daughter is in the health sciences." Pharmacy, Medical Laboratory Science, Physiotherapy, Public Health, Dentistry — plenty of people who came through Biology and are doing well. If it's the actual work — the ward, the patients, the surgery, the 2am calls — then it is worth fighting for Medicine, and you should fight for it properly, with the CGPA and the cut-offs and the faculty on your side.

---

**What I'd actually do if I were you, this week:**

1. **Go to the faculty/department office** and ask the transfer rules for *your* school. Ask the level adviser, ask the faculty secretary, ask them for the written guideline if there is one. Ask: what CGPA, what JAMB cut-off, what post-UTME requirement, how many vacancies, when does the application open, who is on the panel.
2. **Do not trust forum people for this. Including me.** My school's rules are not your school's rules. My adviser is not your adviser. Everything I said above is a starting point, not a source. Please verify all of it.
3. **Decide about the acceptance fee last**, once you have real information instead of two strangers' opinions.
4. **If you accept Biology: get serious about PHY 101 and MTH 101 from day one,** and start with the mindset that you're there for two possible outcomes, not one.
5. **If you rewrite: make it one more attempt, not a habit.** If you sit it again, sit it as if there's no third time.

---

**Last thing.** Tolu, you have been crying since afternoon and it feels like your life ended today. It didn't. I promise you it did not. I know it feels like it, because I locked myself in a room in Surulere and thought exactly that — and I'm sitting here in 100L Biology, I'm doing okay, and I'm still fighting for Medicine, and the world did not end.

Whatever you choose — accept or rewrite, transfer or stay in Biology — you are not ruined, you are not a failure, and you are 19 years old with a whole life in front of you. The people who mess up are the ones who stop moving while they decide.

You're not one of them, because you're asking questions on this forum at 8pm trying to get it right. That's already the difference.

DM me if you want. I'll answer anything. And if you get your school's actual transfer requirements, please post them here — somebody else after you is going to need them.

— *Amaka_Bio100*
